reasons.plausibility: Introducing pores into a metallic alloy almost invariably reduces strength and stiffness, and the claim that pores can maintain or improve mechanical properties at 1000 °C without any strengthening mechanism to compensate for the loss of load-bearing section is physically unsound.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and would decisively falsify the hypothesis, but the hypothesis itself is so fundamentally flawed that the test is not scientifically meaningful.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a method (adding porosity) that is well-known to degrade mechanical properties, especially at high temperatures, and does not address the core challenge of reducing density while maintaining strength.
